channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Gold edges higher as US-Iran diplomacy and weak oil weigh on USD ahead of FOMC meeting
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) opens with a bullish gap at the start of a new week, though it struggles to capitalize on the momentum or find acceptance above the $4,100 mark as bulls seem reluctant ahead of the crucial FOMC meeting, starting on Tuesday.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Holds gains around 186.50 within rising wedge
item.description: EUR/JPY gains ground after registering minor losses in the previous day, trading around 186.50 during the Asian hours on Monday. The currency cross is keeping a bullish near-term bias as it holds above both the nine-period and 50-period Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs).

item.title: Swiss Franc climbs as US Dollar falls on easing safe-haven demand
item.description: USD/CHF depreciates after five days of losses, trading around 0.8150 during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices rose in India on Monday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah weakens as Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo resigns
item.description: USD/IDR has recovered its losses from the previous trading day, hovering around 18,050 during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD jumps over 2% to near $60 on renewed US-Iran diplomacy hopes
item.description: Silver price (XAG) trades sharply higher near $60.00 during the Asian trading session on Monday. The white metal starts the week on a firm note as the pause in military aggression between the United States (US) and Iran has sent oil prices sharply lower.

item.title: United States Dollar Index falls to near 101.00 after US-Iran strike halt
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, is losing ground after posting minor losses in the previous trading day, trading around 101.20 during the Asian session on Monday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar bulls seem hesitant; downside seems limited amid weak USD
item.description: The NZD/USD pair kicks off the new week on a positive note amid a broadly weaker US Dollar (USD), though it struggles to capitalize on gains beyond the 0.5800 mark.

item.title: Canadian Dollar advances as easing risk aversion lifts US Dollar
item.description: USD/CAD depreciates after posting minor gains in the previous trading day, hovering around 1.4080 during the Asian hours on Monday. The pair loses ground as the US Dollar (USD) falls sharply on easing geopolitical tensions following a weekend pause in military hostilities between the US and Iran.

item.title: British Pound strengthens beyond mid-1.3300s vs weak USD amid fresh Iran diplomacy hopes
item.description: The GBP/USD pair builds on Friday's modest bounce from a three-week low and gains strong follow-through positive traction at the start of a new week.

item.title: Gold gains as falling oil prices ease inflation and rate hike fears
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) gains ground for the second consecutive day, trading around 4,103 per troy ounce during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: Euro climbs beyond 1.1400 as renewed Iran diplomacy hopes undermine safe-haven USD
item.description: The EUR/USD pair builds on a modest bullish gap opening and climbs back above the 1.1400 mark during the Asian session on Monday. The intraday move up is sponsored by a broadly weaker US Dollar (USD), weighed down by renewed optimism over a diplomatic resolution to end a five-month-old US-Iran war.

item.title: WTI remains heavily offered near $84.00 amid hopes for de-escalation in US-Iran conflict
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) – the benchmark US Crude Oil price – opens with a bearish gap at the start of a new at the start of a new week and retreats further from its highest level since June 8, around the $92.25 zone, touched last Thursday.

item.title: Japanese Yen gains as oil prices fall after US-Iran strike pause
item.description: USD/JPY remains subdued for the second successive day, trading around 163.60 during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7911 vs. 6.7939 previous
item.description: On Monday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.7911 compared to Friday's fix of 6.7939.

item.title: Middle East War updates: US-Iran pause strikes as Trump weighs up diplomatic options
item.description: Here’s a brief recap of the key developments in the Middle East war that occurred over the weekend, which are expected to have a significant impact on markets in the upcoming week.

item.title: Australian Dollar gains as Mideast tensions ease, RBA rate expectations rise
item.description: AUD/USD extends its gains for the second consecutive trading day, hovering near 0.7000 during the Asian hours on Monday. The pair appreciates as the US Dollar (USD) declines alongside a sharp drop in oil prices.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: MAS seen on hold with cautious inflation tone – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong expect the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) to leave the Singapore Dollar (SGD) Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (S$NEER) policy unchanged at Monday’s meeting despite a modest rebound in core Consumer Price Index (CPI) to 1.6% year-on-year in June.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Cross consolidates under 187.00, bulls target 188.00
item.description: The EUR/JPY consolidates around 186.00, edges down by 0.06% amid a souring of risk appetite amid the escalation of the US-Iran war, and strengthens safe-haven assets like the Japanese Yen.

item.title: Malaysia: Solid fundamentals support Ringgit and bonds – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Chua Han Teng argues that Malaysia’s financial markets reflect confidence in the country’s solid domestic fundamentals despite lingering Middle East geopolitical risks.

item.title: South Korean Won: Strong GDP and inflows support Won – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank reports that South Korea’s advance Q2 GDP rose 0.6% quarter-on-quarter and 3.7% year-on-year, beating expectations. Robust AI-related semiconductor demand and resilient domestic spending underpin growth. The strong data support prospects of a further 25bp Bank of Korea hike in August.

item.title: Forecasting the upcoming week: Fed, BoE and BoJ decisions take center stage
item.description: The upcoming week will be dominated by monetary policy decisions from the Federal Reserve (Fed), Bank of England (BoE) and Bank of Japan (BoJ).

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Kiwi tests 0.5800 as bullish momentum fades
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar gains over 0.30% against the US Dollar on Friday. The pair is poised to test key resistance levels with the 50-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) at 0.5793, slightly below the 0.5800 figure.

item.title: Thai Baht: Oil shock and dovish BoT keep THB pressured against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that the Thai Baht (THB) is trading near its weakest level in more than a year against the US Dollar (USD), as volatile oil prices, a firmer USD and higher US yields weigh on the currency.

item.title: Euro falls even amid strong Eurozone PMIs
item.description: EUR/USD trades lower near the 1.1370 area on Friday, struggling despite stronger-than-expected Eurozone business-activity figures. The US Dollar Index (DXY) remains firmer near 101.50, offering limited support to the pair.

item.title: Gold gains despite firm US Dollar
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) drifts higher on Friday as the Greenback stands firm, even as growing speculation that the US-Iran war may last longer than expected could, in the end, hurt the prospects of the yellow metal. The XAU/USD trades at $4,065, up 0.38%.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: BI pause seen as hawkish hold – UOB
item.description: UOB Global Economics & Markets Research notes that Bank Indonesia kept its policy rate at 5.75%, opting to let earlier tightening filter through.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD consolidates as bulls struggle to clear the 21-day SMA
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) edges higher on Friday as a pullback in Oil prices pushes US Treasury yields lower, while the US Dollar (USD) fluctuates near recent highs. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades around $58.60, up 2.40% on the day.

item.title: The Dow Jones Industrial Average buys a rumour and sleeps through a tariff regime
item.description: The index that spent this week absorbing a war premium trades near 52,000 on Friday, around 325 points to the good side, on the strength of a wire report that its own three sources undercut in the same breath.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Hawkish MAS stance supports SGD – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan expects MAS to keep policy unchanged at the July meeting while maintaining a tightening bias, distinguishing between energy-driven and domestically generated inflation. Strong Singapore growth and a positive output gap justify tight settings.
